why: Nothing in the record proves, refutes, restricts or bounds the Poisson claim about prime divisors of M_p in intervals. Gillies 1964 only states the conjecture (none). Ehrman and Wagstaff 1983 test it numerically over finite exponent ranges (instances, journal-published hence digested). Kovač–Luca use the Gillies heuristic as an input for theorems about f(2n)/f(n), a different quantity; it bears on the problem without settling anything, so none rather than variant. Wagstaff 2025 discusses other Mersenne conjectures with no visible link to Gillies (none); its undated first posting is still placeable after the snapshot because the journal received it in September 2025. Domínguez (τ(p−1)) and Engberg–Pollack (reciprocal divisor sums) are different questions (variant). No AI system is credited anywhere.
doubts: Kovač–Luca's Section 4.2 applies Gillies' model to τ(2^p−1); whether any numerical comparison there tests the interval-distribution claim itself was not settled, but even if it did, it would be a finite-range check (instances). The Wagstaff 2025 PDF was not opened, so a Gillies-related heuristic inside it can't be ruled out entirely.
